title: Theo and the Uniform
premise: Mara Sterling, the quiet driver and letter-reader for suffragist Edith Vance, has learned that survival means knowing everything and saying nothing. When the season's first snow closes the mountain bridge and strands the household, a wounded stranger arrives carrying proof that a beloved local magistrate orchestrated a deadly mill collapse and blamed the workers. Trapped with allies, suspects, and the magistrate's men all under one roof, Mara must choose between protecting Edith and her own anonymity, and putting the truth on record before the magistrate's historians can bury it. The book ends with Mara testifying under her real name — the one she buried years ago — as the bridge reopens and the truth travels out ahead of the victors' pens.
about_author: Paloma Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters never meant to be read. They write from a drafty coastal house, where they claim the fog improves the prose.

chapters.title: The Letters Before the Letters
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Establishes her routine driving for Edith Vance and her private habit of steaming open correspondence, including a letter hinting at trouble at Harrow Mill. Beat: controlled, watchful contentment — a life built on small betrayals of privacy.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. First snow seals the mountain road; the village of Ashenmoor is cut off until spring. Edith insists on staying to finish her campaign work. Beat: unease beneath coziness — the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Stable Door
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A bleeding young man, Tom Alder, collapses in the stable carrying a satchel of documents about the mill collapse. Mara hides him before deciding whether to tell Edith. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Satchel Says
chapters.summary: Mara and Edith's POV, alternating. The documents show Magistrate Corven falsified safety inspections before the collapse that killed nineteen workers. Beat: horror — the truth is heavier than expected.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Men
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Corven's clerk, Mr. Pell, arrives seeking shelter, ostensibly stranded like everyone else. Mara recognizes the danger of a hunter snowed in with his quarry. Beat: dread wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: Edith's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith wants to publish immediately, but the telegraph line is down and her reputation makes her an easy target for dismissal. She asks Mara to copy the documents by hand. Beat: loyalty tested by strategy.

chapters.title: Nineteen Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara interviews villagers about the dead, gathering testimony. Tom's guilt over surviving emerges. Beat: grief becoming evidence; the dead acquire faces.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Kindness
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Pell, disarmingly courteous, probes Mara over cards and whiskey. He reveals he knows someone is hiding in the stable. Beat: cat and mouse; Mara's composure nearly cracks.

chapters.title: The Fire
chapters.summary: Tom's POV. The stable burns in the night — sabotage or accident. Tom escapes with the satchel but is seen by Pell. Beat: panic, loss, the safe harbor burning down.

chapters.title: Accusations
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Pell accuses Edith of harboring a fugitive and an arsonist, threatening her movement's credibility. Edith refuses to yield the documents. Beat: defiance with a cost attached.

chapters.title: Mara's Buried Name
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback: Mara is revealed to be the daughter of a mill worker blacklisted after the collapse — the reason she hides. Beat: the personal wound behind the professional silence.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Snow
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Pell privately offers Mara immunity and passage out if she delivers the satchel to him. Beat: temptation — survival priced in betrayal.

chapters.title: Tom's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tom's POV. Tom recounts the collapse: locked exits, Corven's order to keep the machines running. The household records his sworn statement. Beat: catharsis; testimony becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: The Village Turns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Word leaks; villagers split between fear of Corven and hunger for justice. Some demand the documents to bargain, not publish. Beat: the truth becomes contested territory.

chapters.title: Pell's Mistake
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith baits Pell into revealing Corven ordered the stable fire, witnessed by a servant. Beat: reversal — the hunter leaves a trail.

chapters.title: The Frozen Road
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Pell attempts to leave over the closed bridge with the stolen original documents; Mara intercepts him on the ice. Beat: physical climax of pursuit; near-death on the frozen river.

chapters.title: Corven Arrives
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Corven himself comes through the pass with constables to bury the matter before spring. Beat: the full weight of power arrives at the door.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith stages a public reading of the testimony and the nineteen names in the village hall, with Corven's men watching. Beat: courage as spectacle; truth spoken aloud before witnesses who cannot unhear it.

chapters.title: Pell's Choice
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Confronted with Corven's plan to silence everyone, Pell defects, surrendering Corven's written orders. Beat: the instrument of power turning; loyalty vs. truth resolved in the antagonist's own house.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Thaw comes; constables arrest Corven as the road clears. Mara must decide whether to sign her testimony under her buried name. Beat: the price of survival comes due.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara signs as Mara Sterling, daughter of the blacklisted worker, and hands the full account to a journalist before Corven's allies can shape the story. Beat: climax of identity — anonymity surrendered for permanence.

chapters.title: What the Historians Will Find
chapters.summary: Edith's and Mara's POV in closing alternation. Months later, the inquiry vindicates the nineteen; Mara stays on as Edith's driver but no longer reads the letters — she writes her own. Beat: quiet resolution; belonging earned at cost, truth outrunning the victors' pens.
